QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_41

question.text: For a well-diversified Cat III equity long-only sub-strategy, the Sharpe Ratio and Treynor Ratio will typically give:

answer.text: Identical numbers because they use the same formula
Similar rankings because, in a well-diversified portfolio, unsystematic risk is small and β ≈ σ/σ_market
Treynor will always be higher than Sharpe

explanation.text: The Logic: For well-diversified portfolios, unsystematic risk is small, so total standard deviation is dominated by the systematic component (β ≈ σ/σ_market). As a result, Sharpe (uses σ) and Treynor (uses β) give similar rankings. Undiversified portfolios can produce different rankings between the two ratios. The Trap: Option A overstates divergence. Option B confuses the formulas. Option D states an arbitrary inequality. Note: The workbook explicitly notes the well-diversified case where Sharpe and Treynor produce similar results, and the undiversified case where they can diverge.
